workarounds.symptom: load_from_url includes URL query strings and fragments in the file suffix, misrouting PDF responses
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(rag): strip URL query/fragment before deriving file suffix in load_from_url. Target files: api/core/rag/extractor/extract_processor.py, api/tests/unit_tests/core/rag/extractor/test_extract_processor.py. `ExtractProcessor.load_from_url` derived the temp file suffix with `Path(url).suffix`. For URLs carrying a query string or fragment (e.g. `https://example.com/doc.pdf?token=abc` or `...#page=2`), the query/fragment leaked into the suffix (`.pdf?token=abc`), so the extractor dispatch in `extract()` never matched `.pdf` an... workarounds.symptom: Bug] Agent node fails with TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len() — canvas writes unset strategy params as {variable, null}, runtime crashes on them
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(agent): treat null variable value as unset strategy param. Target files: api/core/workflow/nodes/agent/runtime_support.py, api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/nodes/agent/test_runtime_support.py. An Agent node with optional strategy params left unset (files, allowed_tools) failed on every run. The canvas stores those params as {"type": "variable", "value": null}, and build_parameters passed the null selector to variable_pool.get, which raised TypeError: object of type NoneType has no len(). (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/45904)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Empty attachment IDs can break knowledge retrieval history
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: validate retrieval attachment UUIDs and tolerate invalid image history. Target files: api/controllers/console/datasets/hit_testing_base.py, api/repositories/knowledge/dataset_read_repository.py, packages/contracts/generated/api/console/datasets/zod.gen.ts. Knowledge retrieval accepts `attachment_ids: [""]` and can persist the empty ID in query history. When history is loaded later, the value reaches a PostgreSQL UUID query and causes the whole history list to fail. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/45915)

Fix: fix(docker): initialize plugin daemon storage permissions. Target files: docker/docker-compose-template.yaml, docker/docker-compose.yaml. Since plugin daemon 0.6.12 the container runs as the `dify` user (uid 1001), but `./volumes/plugin_daemon` is created by Docker as root on a fresh install, and on upgraded installs it still holds files written by the old root daemon. So plugin installs fail with `mkdir /app/storage/assets: permission denied`. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/45615)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the f
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the file size limit, so a plugin claiming an absurd size crashed the worker with `MemoryError` — the 30 MB limit was never consulted. The declared size is now validated first and rejected with the documented size-limit error. (#42021). Upstream PR #42021. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/42021)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built-in web scraper whenever a target returns `Content-Type: application/pdf` — asserted on an upload record that URL loads never have. Tenant context is now optional, image extraction is skipped when it is absent, and text extraction works again. (#41950). Upstream PR #41950. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/41950)
